label: Landscaping
title: Garden Design & Landscaping in Newquay
description: I provide practical garden design in Newquay and landscaping across Cornwall for homeowners who want a better layout without an overcomplicated process. Whether you want a gravel garden, new planting beds, turf or a smarter space that is easier to look after, I plan the work around your site, budget and coastal conditions. I grew up on a farm in Tasmania, so working outdoors and shaping land is second nature to me. Every scope and quote is clear before I start.

included.label: What’s included
included.title: The details that make it feel done properly
included.description: Landscaping in Cornwall does not have to mean a massive project or a five-figure budget. Most of my work involves focused improvements that make a real, visible difference without tearing everything up. I will walk the garden with you, talk through what is realistic, and suggest changes that suit Cornwall’s climate and your soil type. Coastal gardens near Newquay or Perranporth often need salt-tolerant planting schemes and windbreaks, while gardens further inland around Truro tend to have heavier clay soils that benefit from better drainage and raised bed design. I plan around all of that so nothing gets installed and then struggles.

items.title: Bed shaping & edging
items.description: Clean, defined lines that make the whole garden feel intentional. I reshape borders to suit the natural contours of your plot and create crisp edges between lawn and beds. In Cornwall's mild climate, growth is fast, so well-defined bed shapes make ongoing maintenance far simpler.

items.title: Planting & replanting
items.description: I choose plants that genuinely suit your conditions rather than picking whatever looks good on the day. For coastal Cornwall gardens, that often means hebe, escallonia, pittosporum, and ornamental grasses. These handle salt winds well and look good year-round. Inland around Bodmin or Truro, I lean towards varieties that cope with heavier soil and more moisture.

items.title: Mulching & soil improvement
items.description: Cornwall's soils vary a lot across the county. Sandy, free-draining soil near the coast benefits from composted organic matter to improve moisture retention. Clay-heavy soil around Truro needs careful amendment to avoid waterlogging. I work in quality mulch and compost to give new planting the best possible start, and it gives beds a much more polished, finished appearance.

items.title: Lawn prep & turfing
items.description: Proper ground preparation is the difference between a lawn that establishes quickly and one that struggles. I level the area, improve the soil underneath, and lay quality turf that suits Cornwall's year-round growing season. Because lawns here rarely go fully dormant, you will see results faster than you might expect.

items.title: Hedge shaping & structure tidy-up
items.description: Hedges and structural plants give a garden its shape and sense of boundary. I prune and reshape them to create a crisp, tidy outline that frames the rest of the space. I can handle larger overgrown hedging that needs cutting back before reshaping, and I will flag anything that needs a specialist tree surgeon.

items.title: Seasonal refresh & waste removal
items.description: Green waste can be cleared from site as agreed in the quote. Quilliams is an Environment Agency registered waste carrier (lower tier), CBDL582202. Green waste removal is charged at £10 per dumpy bag, and I include the expected route and cost in the quote so there are no surprises.

valueBand.label: Value
valueBand.title: Improvements that add real value
valueBand.description: I focus on landscaping changes that feel worth the investment, both immediately and in the longer term. A well-planned gravel garden, for example, typically costs between £1,500 and £2,500 and takes 2 to 3 days, but it can transform an awkward or high-maintenance space into something you actually enjoy using. I always recommend improvements that suit Cornwall's growing conditions, so the results hold up through salty coastal winters and damp inland seasons alike.

bullets.title: Looks finished
bullets.description: Defined edges, considered planting, and a coherent layout give the garden a finished quality you notice straight away. Most customers say it feels like a different space within the first week.

bullets.title: Easier upkeep
bullets.description: Smarter plant choices and better bed layout reduce the time you spend weeding, watering, and cutting back. I plan for Cornwall's fast growth rate so the garden stays manageable between visits.

bullets.title: Done properly
bullets.description: You get a clear, fixed quote before any work begins. I outline exactly what is included, what materials cost, and how long the job will take. No vague estimates or surprise extras at the end.

faq.label: FAQs
faq.title: Quick answers
faq.description: If you don’t see your question here, just get in touch.

items.question: Do you help with design ideas?
items.answer: Yes, I am happy to help with design ideas. Many customers have a rough vision of what they want but need help working out the practical details. I can suggest layouts, materials, and planting schemes based on your space, your budget, and how much time you want to spend maintaining the finished result. I take into account Cornwall’s coastal climate and soil conditions so that whatever I suggest will actually thrive here. I keep things practical rather than overcomplicating it. If you already have a clear plan, I can work from that too.

items.question: Can you work with what I already have?
items.answer: Absolutely. Not every landscaping job is a blank canvas, and many of the projects I take on involve improving or reworking what is already there. That might mean reshaping borders, adding new planting around existing features, improving drainage, or replacing tired surfaces. Working with existing elements often keeps costs down and avoids the disruption of a full redesign. I will always let you know if something existing is worth keeping or if it makes more sense to start fresh in a particular area.

items.question: How long does a landscaping job take?
items.answer: It depends on the scope. A straightforward job like creating a new border or laying a small patio area might take 1 to 2 days. Larger projects involving ground preparation, planting, and hard landscaping can take anywhere from a few days to a couple of weeks. I will give you a realistic timeframe before starting so you know what to expect. Cornwall’s weather can occasionally cause short delays during wetter months, but I plan around that and always keep you updated if anything changes.

items.question: Do you remove waste?
items.answer: Waste removal can be included where agreed. Green waste removal is charged at £10 per dumpy bag, and other materials such as rubble or old fencing need a suitable route priced for that material. Quilliams is an Environment Agency registered waste carrier (lower tier), CBDL582202. I set out the expected waste route and cost in the quote before work begins.

items.question: Can you recommend low-maintenance plants?
items.answer: Yes, and this is something I get asked about a lot. Cornwall’s mild coastal climate gives you a wider range of options than most of the UK, which is a real advantage. For low-maintenance gardens, I often suggest hardy shrubs like hebe, escallonia, and pittosporum, along with ground cover plants that suppress weeds naturally. Ornamental grasses also do well here and need very little attention. I match recommendations to your soil type, how much sun the area gets, and whether it is exposed to coastal wind. The aim is a garden that looks good without constant fussing.
